transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good afternoon, thank you for calling S-Net Mobile Upgrades and Billing Support. My name is Freya speaking today. How may I help you?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good afternoon Freya. My name is Cordelia, and I'm calling because my £180 trade-in credit for my old iPhone 13 still hasn't been applied to my mobile bill, even though your warehouse received the phone twenty-one days ago.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Hi Cordelia, I would be glad to look into your iPhone 13 trade-in and get your mobile bill sorted out today. Before I access your account, could you please confirm your billing postcode and address along with your four-digit security PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, of course. My address is 27 Montague Square, Bath, BA1 2LZ, and my four-digit security PIN is 8521.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you very much, Cordelia. Your address and PIN are verified and I have your S-Net Mobile account open in front of me.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thanks Freya. When I upgraded to the iPhone 16 Pro last month, I was guaranteed £180 off my first full upgrade bill as long as I returned my old 128-gigabyte Midnight iPhone 13 within fourteen days in good working condition.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I posted it in the padded S-Net trade-in pack using Royal Mail Tracked 24, and the tracking shows the warehouse signed for it twenty-one days ago on the twenty-seventh of September.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yet my October mobile bill just came out this morning for £215.00—which includes the £180 upfront device balance that the trade-in was supposed to wipe out plus my £35.00 monthly airtime plan!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am so sorry for the frustration and shock of seeing a £215.00 bill when you sent your iPhone 13 back right on time three weeks ago, Cordelia—I completely understand why you want that £180 credit sorted before your Direct Debit goes out.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So just to make sure I have all the details straight: you returned your 128-gigabyte iPhone 13 via Royal Mail Tracked 24, it was signed for at the trade-in warehouse 21 days ago on 27 September, but the £180 trade-in credit was not applied to today's £215.00 bill.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that is 100 percent accurate, Freya. My Direct Debit is scheduled for the twenty-fourth of October and I really don't want £215.00 leaving my current account.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let's trace the exact warehouse parcel record right now, Cordelia. Do you happen to have the Royal Mail Tracked 24 reference number and the last four digits of your old iPhone 13's IMEI number from your trade-in confirmation email?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, I have the email open on my laptop right here! The Royal Mail Tracked 24 number is JB482910385GB, and the old iPhone 13 IMEI ends in 8492.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for having both of those ready. Could I also check whether you turned off Find My iPhone and Activation Lock before sealing the iPhone 13 in the return pack, and whether you received any grading query email?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, I signed out of iCloud completely, turned off Find My iPhone, and did a full factory reset while I was still in the Bath S-Net store, and no, I haven't received any emails asking about grading.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me search the trade-in portal using Royal Mail tracking JB482910385GB and IMEI ending 8492 right now, Cordelia.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you, Freya. I hope it hasn't been lost in a corner somewhere after being signed for.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good news—the phone is definitely not lost! I can see your Midnight iPhone 13 with IMEI ending 8492 was scanned into the receiving bay on 27 September at 10:18 AM.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Even better, the technician completed the physical and diagnostic check on 30 September: Find My iPhone Off, Battery Health 89%, Screen and Housing Grade A, Approved Value £180.00.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait—if it passed the inspection on the thirtieth of September for the full £180.00, why on earth wasn't the £180.00 credit applied to my October bill?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Looking at the voucher batch log, after the technician marked your IMEI ending 8492 as Grade A Approved on 30 September, the warehouse batch file failed to push the settlement webhook back to S-Net's billing ledger, leaving your voucher stuck in 'Pending Warehouse Export' status.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So it's just been sitting stuck in a computer queue since the thirtieth of September?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, and because our fourteen-working-day SLA has already passed and I can see the Grade A pass for £180.00 right here on the portal, I am going to manually override the stuck batch and credit the £180.00 directly onto your S-Net Mobile bill right now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh, thank goodness! Will that reduce the £215.00 Direct Debit that is due to come out on the twenty-fourth of October, or would it only go onto November's bill?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Because today is 18 October and your Direct Debit collection file isn't locked until 72 hours before 24 October, applying an immediate billing adjustment recalculates your live October invoice and updates the Direct Debit collection amount to £35.00!

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is music to my ears, Freya. Paying £35.00 for my normal monthly plan instead of £215.00 is a huge relief.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you see on the portal what condition notes the technician wrote when they tested my old iPhone 13 on the thirtieth of September?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, I can read the line items from the diagnostic feed: LCD Display Pass, Face ID Sensor Pass, Rear Camera Module Pass, Water Ingress Indicator Negative, and Zero Cosmetic Cracks.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I kept that iPhone 13 in an OtterBox case with a tempered glass screen protector from day one, so I knew it was spotless!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It really shows from the diagnostic scores, Cordelia—89 percent battery health after two years is well above the 80 percent Grade A threshold.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Why did the October bill charge the £180.00 as a lump sum in the first place instead of spreading it across the contract?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: When you choose the Guaranteed Trade-In Upfront Offset option during an upgrade, the system defers the £180.00 upfront hardware contribution for 30 days to give your old handset time to reach the warehouse.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Normally, once the warehouse scan approves the handset within 14 days, the £180.00 credit cancels out that deferred hardware charge before the first bill prints.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Ah, I see! So because the warehouse export got stuck in the queue after the thirtieth of September, the billing system thought I hadn't completed the trade-in and billed me the £180.00 upfront hardware charge!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is the exact mechanism, Cordelia. Your handset arrived well within the 14-day window, so you did everything right on your end.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And does manually overriding the voucher today affect my 24-month upgrade contract term or my AppleCare warranty at all?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Not at all—your 24-month contract start date of 18 September and your device warranty remain completely unchanged.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And there won't be any late payment fee or admin charge added because the £180.00 was sitting on the bill until today?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: No, because your bill was only generated this morning and payment isn't due until 24 October, there are zero late fees or credit-file markers of any kind.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Phew, that is a relief.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am keying in the £180.00 Trade-In Settlement Override against trade-in order TI-903412 and IMEI ending 8492 right now, Cordelia.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: While you are doing that, could you also send me a copy of the official physical handset inspection and data-wipe certificate from the warehouse for my records? My employer reimburses part of my phone upgrade if I show the trade-in grading certificate.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Honestly, our third-party grading contractor Assurant is a shambles—that's their mess not ours, and if you have any query about the physical handset inspection certificate you'll have to chase Assurant directly because I don't deal with their warehouse.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh, really? I assumed since I traded the phone in through S-Net, S-Net could issue the grading certificate, or at least request it from them.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yeah, Assurant runs the warehouse under their own system, so we only get the one-line electronic feed in our portal. What I CAN send you from S-Net is an itemized VAT credit note showing the £180.00 trade-in settlement against IMEI ending 8492.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, well, the itemized S-Net credit note showing the £180.00 trade-in settlement and the IMEI should hopefully satisfy our finance department at work.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have made sure the credit note narrative explicitly states: 'Approved Grade A Trade-In Settlement — Apple iPhone 13 128GB Midnight (IMEI ending 8492, Royal Mail JB482910385GB) — £180.00'.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Having the model, storage size, Royal Mail tracking number, and IMEI printed right on the credit note is actually really helpful.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And I have also closed out the open trade-in reminder flag on your upgrade agreement so our automated system never sends you any 'reminder to return your old device' texts.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh, I am glad you checked that! My colleague got chased by automated texts for a month after returning her phone.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, when a warehouse export gets stuck like yours did, the automated reminder loop can trigger on day 25 if we don't manually mark the return obligation as Fulfilled, so I have locked yours as Fulfilled and Closed.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you for thinking ahead on that, Freya. Has the £180.00 adjustment gone through onto my live bill now?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It has just committed on the billing ledger, Cordelia! I have pushed a real-time sync to your My S-Net Mobile app and sent the PDF credit note to your email.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: If you have your iPhone 16 Pro handy, could you open the My S-Net app, pull down to refresh the Billing tab, and check what your live balance and Direct Debit amount show?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me open the My S-Net app on my mobile right now and pull down on the Billing screen...

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh, brilliant! Where it said £215.00 ten minutes ago, it now says Current Balance: £35.00, and right underneath it says Trade-In Credit Applied: -£180.00!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And if you tap on 'Upcoming Direct Debit — 24 October' right below that balance, does it confirm the updated collection figure of £35.00?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Tapping on Upcoming Direct Debit now... Yes! It says '£35.00 to be collected by Direct Debit on 24 October 2026'.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And my email just pinged on my laptop—the PDF credit note CN-7721904 has arrived with the full iPhone 13 128GB Midnight details and IMEI ending 8492 on it!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That means your October Direct Debit is locked in at £35.00, your trade-in obligation is marked Fulfilled, and you have the PDF credit note ready for your employer, Cordelia.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And from November onwards, my normal monthly bill will just be the £35.00 unlimited 5G tariff as agreed?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is right, Cordelia—£35.00 per month on the 24th of each month with no remaining upfront device balance.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What is the reference number for the manual override you did today, just so I can keep it with the PDF credit note?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Your support case reference is MOB-6638102, which is linked directly to credit note CN-7721904 on your account history.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me type MOB-6638102 into my spreadsheet next to the credit note number... Done.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there anything else at all I can help you with on your new iPhone 16 Pro or your S-Net Mobile account today, Cordelia?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Actually, one quick question—did my visual voicemail and Wi-Fi calling carry over automatically when my SIM transferred to the iPhone 16 Pro?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me check your network provisioning profile right now... Yes, both 5G Standalone, Wi-Fi Calling, and Apple Visual Voicemail are active on your eSIM profile.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Awesome, I noticed Wi-Fi Calling was working in my kitchen yesterday where the stone walls are thick, so it's good to know Visual Voicemail is active too.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And your EU Roaming Pass up to 30 gigabytes is also included in that £35.00 plan whenever you travel.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh lovely, I am going to Lisbon for a long weekend in November so that will come in handy!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You will be completely covered in Portugal at no extra cost, Cordelia.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you so much for sorting out the £180.00 credit on the spot today, Freya. That took a huge weight off my mind.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It was my pleasure getting that £180.00 credit applied for you, Cordelia. Thank you for choosing S-Net Mobile, and if you have a moment for the brief text survey after our call, I would really appreciate your feedback.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I will fill out the text survey as soon as it comes through. Have a lovely afternoon, Freya!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you, Cordelia, enjoy your new iPhone and your upcoming trip to Lisbon. Goodbye!
